title: Left semibraces, near left semibraces and the Yang-Baxter equation
summary: A triple $(S, +, \cdot)$ is called a {\em left semibrace} if $(S, +)$ is a semigroup, $(S, \cdot)$ is a group with identity $e$ and $x(y+z)=(xy)+(x(x^{-1}+z))$ for all $x, y, z\in S$, where $x^{-1}$ is the inverse of $x$ in the group $(S, \cdot)$. A left semibrace $(S,+,\cdot)$ is called {\em strong} if $x+y(e+z)=x+yz$ for all $x, y, z\in S$. Left semibraces and strong left semibraces are investigated extensively in literature.
